hints: Look at what HCN does to a C=O bond, think about which ion actually attacks the slightly positive carbon.
Work backwards from the cyanohydrin product, the central carbon has $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$, $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$, so X must have had those two alkyl groups joined by C=O.
Connect the two ideas, an attack by a negative ion means one type of addition, and two carbon groups on C=O means one type of carbonyl.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the product as a cyanohydrin**

This product has both $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$ on the same carbon. That is the classic signature of HCN adding across a C=O double bond.

General change:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)}$$

**Decide the mechanism: nucleophilic addition**

The C=O bond is polar, with $\text{C}^{\delta+}$ and $\text{O}^{\delta-}$. The nucleophile $\text{CN}^-$ is attracted to the $\text{C}^{\delta+}$ and donates a pair of electrons to it.

Because a nucleophile attacks and adds across the double bond, this is nucleophilic addition, not electrophilic addition.

**Work back to find X: ketone, not aldehyde**

Remove $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$ from the product carbon and put back C=O. The carbon is left joined to $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$.

So X is:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COC}_4\text{H}_9$$
A carbonyl with two alkyl groups is a ketone. An aldehyde would need at least one H directly on the C=O carbon.

options.A: Incorrect on both parts. The attack is by CN-, a nucleophile, on the delta positive carbon, so it is not electrophilic addition. X has two alkyl groups, not an aldehyde H.
options.B: Half right about ketone but wrong about mechanism. Students sometimes think addition to a double bond must be electrophilic like in alkenes, but C=O is polar and is attacked by nucleophiles.
options.C: Correct about nucleophilic addition but wrong about the carbonyl type. An aldehyde product would have one H and only one alkyl group on the central carbon, but here we see $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$.
options.D: Correct. CN- acts as a nucleophile adding to the C=O carbon, so nucleophilic addition. Working backwards gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COC}_4\text{H}_9$, a ketone with two alkyl groups.
